correctness.rationale: Countervaluation at a missing R^(m+k)-successor verifies the frame correspondence Box^(m+k)p -> Box^m p iff R^m subset R^(m+k). The count of distinct injective length-m paths has mean (n)_(m+1)p^m -> c^m; overlapping path unions have at least m+1 arcs on at most e+1 vertices, so all non-disjoint factorial-moment contributions vanish and Z_n=>Pois(c^m). Additional arcs at any path vertex have expectation O(n^(-1/m)); all short directed cycles and length-(m+k) walks vanish whp. Isolated m-paths then require exactly one deleted existing arc apiece and offer m choices, giving D=Z_n, H=m^Z_n. The subcritical and intermediate regimes follow first/second moment arguments and fixed p>0 dense validity uses many arc-disjoint candidates. A separate exact 64-frame enumeration for 3 vertices, m=2,k=1 independently confirmed all valuation/frame equivalences and exact deletion minimizers; this is not a proof of the asymptotic limit.
residual_risks: The limit assumes fixed m>=2,k>=1,c>0 and iid loop-free directed arcs; nontrivial denser vanishing-p windows outside the specified regimes are not classified.
Finite enumeration confirms correspondence and deletion counting only at small n.

value.rationale: A motivated, complete critical-window repair-count distribution and a sharp validity transition for a natural modal reduction axiom on sparse random Kripke frames. The pair (minimum edits, count of optimal solutions) is more informative than the classical probability of a rare path and has distinct modal semantics and algorithmic interpretation.
residual_risks: Generality restricted to one modal axiom family and uniform independent arc deletion; still a natural model.
